findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued default is evaluated at class definition time, not per instance
findings.body: In the AssignmentSource dataclass, `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates `timezone.now()` exactly once when the module is imported, and that single value becomes the default for every instance created without an explicit `queued` argument. Every AssignmentSource produced by `from_integration` (and every one reconstructed by `from_dict` when the serialized payload omits `queued`) will therefore share the same timestamp — the process startup time, not the actual time the assignment was queued. This silently breaks the semantic of the field and any future logic that relies on it (ordering, staleness checks, debugging). Use `dataclasses.field(default_factory=lambda: timezone.now())` so a fresh timestamp is computed per instance.

findings.title: Outbound deassign cycle-break path is not covered by tests
findings.body: The PR adds `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration` to verify that outbound `assign` is suppressed when the AssignmentSource matches the target integration. There is no symmetric test for outbound `deassign` (`GroupAssignee.objects.deassign(group, assignment_source=...)`) being suppressed. The `deassign` method also forwards `assignment_source` to `sync_group_assignee_outbound`, so the cycle-break logic on the unassignment path is exercised by no test, and a regression there would silently re-introduce the sync loop on unassign events.

findings.title: No test verifies inbound change still propagates to other integrations on the same group
findings.body: The PR description claims the change 'should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward', but the new tests only assert that the source integration is suppressed. There is no test that links a single group to two different integrations and confirms that an inbound change from integration A still triggers an outbound sync to integration B. Without that test, a future change that, for example, compares `sync_source` against the group or organization instead of the integration_id could silently break multi-installation setups.

findings.title: sync_status_outbound signature accepts assignment_source but no caller or implementation passes it
findings.body: The abstract method `sync_status_outbound` is updated to accept `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None`, but neither any caller in this PR nor any concrete implementation is updated to pass it. The status-sync path is left in an inconsistent state: the parameter is declared but unused. If the intent is to apply the same cycle-break to status syncs, the wiring (callers + concrete implementations) is incomplete and the fix is half-done; if the intent is only a placeholder, the parameter should not be added in this PR. Either finish the wiring or revert this signature update so future maintainers are not misled.
